messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The baseline model, which is the unconditional LSTM, performs with an unlabelled F1 score of 38.5." -- cites: E5 (Section Table 1): quote "Unconditional 38.5 31.7"
2. "The AMR-to-parse model performs worse than the Text-to-parse model in terms of unlabelled F1 score, with a score of 60.4 compared to 87.5 for the Text-to-parse model." -- cites: E5 (Section Table 1): quote "Model Unlabelled F1 Labelled F1 Text-to-parse 87.5 85.8 AMR-to-parse 60.4 54.8"

Cited evidence:
[E5] (text, Section Table 1, page 4): Table 1: Parsing scores on LDC2017T10 dev set. Model Unlabelled F1 Labelled F1 Text-to-parse 87.5 85.8 AMR-to-parse 60.4 54.8 Unconditional 38.5 31.7

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E5 (Section Table 1) shows that the unconditional LSTM model has an unlabelled F1 score of 38.5, which matches the claim.

The evidence in E5 (Section Table 1) shows that the AMR-to-parse model has an unlabelled F1 score of 60.4 and the Text-to-parse model has an unlabelled F1 score of 87.5. This supports the claim that the AMR-to-parse model performs worse than the Text-to-parse model in terms of unlabelled F1 score.
